acceptance: With the wave 130 LOOP_ORCH signal sequence, wave status prints width 1/4, not 3/4 (red test first)
A cycle whose lane hit LOOP_ORCH_LANE_DEADLINE shows as stopped by the deadline, never as a live phase
wave-operations.md states where the width comes from
fix: TDD first with the wave 130 signal sequence as a fixture (red test: status reports width 1/4 and cycles 1955 and 1957 as stopped by the deadline). Update docs/operations/wave-operations.md and the package notes. 100% coverage on changed functions, zero comments.
summary: In wave 130 the lane deadline (LOOP_ORCH_LANE_DEADLINE, 2h7m) killed cycles 1955 (02:02Z) and 1957 (03:00Z). Their cycle state stayed 'phase build', so evolve wave status kept listing them as running and printed 'width 3/4 · utilization 0.83' while the pool ran live=1 of 4 for three hours (LOOP_ORCH_POOL_IDLE fields.live=1 target=4). The operator found the stall before the console did. wave status must take the live lane count and the per-lane state from the pool's LOOP_ORCH_* signals (launched, exited, deadline, late-exit), and a lane stopped by its deadline must leave a sealed, labelled outcome for its cycle (for example 'stopped: lane deadline') instead of a live phase.
title: wave status counts live lanes from the pool, and a deadline-killed lane seals its cycle
